title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: To a team lead who rewards what can be seen: you are judging the loaves at the oven, and by then the bread is already decided.
Here is what the work before the oven looks like: the month of feeding the starter, with nothing to show for it.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.0: the month of feeding the starter

nodes.text: And this is what it looks like kept up for years: the eleven years of notebooks.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.1: the eleven years of notebooks

nodes.text: Someone who knew the craft saw it in the slow work: "That was the moment she knew he would be good." You can learn to look there too.
The ask: protect the unglamorous early work on your team before it has anything to show.
Who is the letter to: one real lead, or a general "you"? And what prompts it now? The brief names the audience but no occasion.
What specific thing is the reader asked to do? A letter's ask needs to be concrete, and the brief only gives the purpose.
